bug_semantics: devalue 5.6.3 added a SPARSE-array decoding branch shared by parse() and unflatten(). It accepted attacker-controlled array lengths and keys, then assigned array[idx] without requiring idx to be an in-range non-negative integer. A key of __proto__ therefore invoked Array.prototype's inherited __proto__ setter, allowing attacker-controlled prototype chains that cause denial of service or type confusion.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable SPARSE decoder was first written by 819f1ac7475ab37547645cfb09bf2f678a799cf0; its verified parent 0f04d4d678eac39ad5d7a07d1956275d7874e81c has no SPARSE constant or decoding branch.

evidence: 819f1ac7475ab37547645cfb09bf2f678a799cf0 adds SPARSE=-7 and the unflatten branch that creates Array(len) and performs array[idx] = hydrate(...) with no key, integer, sign, or bounds validation.
0f04d4d678eac39ad5d7a07d1956275d7874e81c is the sole parent of the BIC and lacks both SPARSE and the vulnerable branch; 819f1ac7475ab37547645cfb09bf2f678a799cf0 is contained in v5.6.3 but not v5.6.2.
The GitHub advisory identifies affected version 5.6.3, patched version 5.6.4, and prototype pollution in parse/unflatten leading to denial of service or type confusion.

40f1db13afdd65c8e2ebd02f684276c273ef81b0 directly fixes the SPARSE path by requiring len and idx to be non-negative integers and idx < len before assignment, with regression cases for __proto__, CPU exhaustion, and type confusion.

Annotated tag v5.6.3 (tag object 37c577685cdbf90a59351d49f92249c8bb68e12a) resolves to release commit a4a37d208a4d1bdd0d58c82e5644c87cab855259 containing the BIC; annotated tag v5.6.4 (tag object c556b7aa38cf0b45d7072f9738a8099c19f4a25e) resolves to 6cbb3f51258e01d7769e2b3d77b6ce9ed060804b containing the direct fix.
